quality.note: Missing required context remains withheld. This gate does not establish semantic truth or useful coverage.

findings: Held-out validation shows 110/110 records emitted for party_key, party_name and party_kind with 0 rejected values, and 47/110 for abn_supplied with 0 rejected values; the 63 blanks are deliberate abstention on a frequently-missing source attribute, not incorrect emissions.

Semantic separation is defensible: party_key is explicitly not an ABN/ACN or legal-entity assertion; party_name is explicitly not a registered legal or trading name; party_kind is explicitly a party classification with no legal-form, sole-trader or beneficial-ownership implication; abn_supplied is explicitly unvalidated and its absence is explicitly not evidence of no business or no Australian presence.

Owner separation is correct: all four concepts are owned by the party role, not by business, so entity.abn, entity.acn, entity.legal_name, entity.trading_name, entity.entity_type, ext.entity.legal_form and ext.entity.holder_kind are not reused where reuse would change meaning or owner.

Grain and identity cautions are consistent with the inspection: party_id alone does not identify a unique business relationship (roles vary across rows), and application-level status/dates/description are correctly excluded from this group's columns.
Enum mapping is bounded: only 'organisation' and 'individual' map, with unlisted values becoming missing rather than guessed; held-out examples confirm both values pass through unchanged.

Privacy handling is honest: party_name is marked personal_data=always and the mapping rationale states it is suppressed from profile views for the mixed person/organisation population, with the lost utility acknowledged rather than hidden.
No population-accuracy or completeness claim is made; the cohort is described as a patent-prefix subset and the quality gate note states it does not establish semantic truth or useful coverage.
No invented fallback dates or hypothetical guards are required; observed_at uses resource_last_modified fallback, which is observation-at-retrieval and is not described as a publisher-stated update.
semantic_risks: party_name values in held-out examples include digit strings (e.g. '2611463834', '9010020818') classified as individual parties; these are party labels as published, not names, and downstream consumers must not treat them as person names or as identifiers.
abn_supplied is stored as a string without checksum validation; a non-11-digit or malformed supplied value would pass through unchanged, so consumers must not treat it as a validated ABN.
party_kind is a party classification only; a value of 'organisation' must not be read as a company legal form, and 'individual' must not be read as sole-trader status.

party_key is a publisher party identifier; the same organisation may appear under multiple party_ids and the same party_id may hold different roles across rows, so it must not be used as a business entity key.
The 42.7% coverage on abn_supplied reflects source blanks, not a mapping defect; any downstream completeness metric must not interpret the blanks as absence of an Australian business.
checked_reuse: entity.abn — rejected: validated business-owned identifier; abn_supplied is unvalidated, often-missing party-record attribute whose absence is not evidence.
entity.acn — rejected: checksummed company registration with different owner and meaning than an IP-office party key.
entity.legal_name — rejected: asserts registered legal name; party_name is an unverified, lower-cased IP-office party label.
entity.trading_name — rejected: asserts trading status; party_name makes no such assertion.
entity.entity_type — rejected: asserts business legal structure; party_kind is a party-level organisation/individual flag with no legal-form implication.
ext.entity.legal_form — rejected: asserts business legal form; party_kind explicitly does not.
ext.entity.holder_kind — rejected: business-owned matching evidence about a licence/registration holder, a different meaning and owner than a party classification on an IP application record.
critic.rationale: The group's four concepts are semantically defensible, correctly owned by the party role, and explicitly bounded against legal-form, legal-identity, validation and population claims. Held-out validation shows full coverage with zero rejected values on the three fully-present fields and honest partial coverage (47/110) on the frequently-blank ABN field, with blanks treated as deliberate abstention rather than incorrect emissions. Reuse checks confirm that business-owned identifiers and legal-form concepts were not inappropriately reused. No blocking semantic, owner, unit, date, legal-claim or provenance defect was found in the emitted claims; the remaining risks are consumer-interpretation cautions, not mapping or ontology errors. This is an automated critique, not human approval.
